title: Three-Tier Enforcement Classification as Methodology-Level Taxonomy
summary: Adopts the Three-Tier Enforcement Classification as the methodology-level taxonomy operationalizing Invariant 8's anchoring requirement: Skill-Structure Layer (step-anchored dispatch in skill text, ADR-065), Harness Layer (PostToolUse dispatch log plus Stop hook manifest compound check, ADR-063/064), and User-Tooling Layer (graduating conversational mechanisms to artifact-producing form, ADR-066). A mechanism proposal is classified by a four-step decision procedure; one that fits none of the three substrates cannot be specified as unconditional (Tier 1) and must be marked best-effort or contingent instead. The three substrates are not a priority hierarchy — each is primary in its own domain — and a single mechanism may legitimately be anchored to more than one substrate at once.
workflow_point: cross-cutting — classification procedure for any new Tier 1 mechanism proposal
mechanism: three-substrate taxonomy with a four-step classification decision procedure

supersession.text: ADR-089 amends the Harness Layer row's enforcement-technique description and the decision-procedure step 2 language to reflect ADR-088's advisory demotion (v0.8.3). The Three-Tier substrate framing, the four-step decision procedure structure, and the substrate primacy ordering all remain current authority. Only the Harness Layer's enforcement-technique description and the State-C claim language are amended (block → advisory; impossibility → detectability).
